fatal_errors: The proposed agglomeration intervention does not reconstruct the demonstrated low-temperature ID-HVAF i7 process and optimized medium air/fuel setting.

The cited evidence only discusses particle-size-dependent melting and splat formation in atmospheric plasma spraying; it does not support pre-sintering, reduced oxidation, increased deposition thickness, or use of 45–75 μm agglomerates.

The assertion that larger agglomerates will melt and spread better is not established and may be reversed under unchanged spray conditions because larger particles can remain partially molten and rebound.
No relevant bond-coat service regime or oxidation test is specified, so preservation of integrity and protective alumina formation at 1000–1150 °C cannot be evaluated.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the thickness shortfall and proposes a single, testable feedstock modification, but it substantially diverges from the target intervention. The target used optimized low-temperature ID-HVAF spraying to produce an approximately 150 μm, 0.2%-porosity coating with minimal deposition oxidation and a continuous alumina TGO during 50 h exposures at 1000–1150 °C. The generated hypothesis instead assumes that sintered 45–75 μm agglomerates will improve melting, spreading, and deposition under unspecified conventional spray conditions. That mechanism is weakly supported and potentially problematic because larger or porous agglomerates may heat less uniformly, remain partially molten, or introduce internal porosity. The proposed experiment has useful controls and a clear falsification rule for thickness and as-sprayed integrity, but it lacks deposition-efficiency measurements, defined torch parameters, and high-temperature oxidation/TGO testing needed to establish bond-coat service performance. Thus it is novel and experimentally testable, but not adequately supported as a scientifically grounded alternative.
